newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia imposes tough punishment on illegal aliens.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia imposes tough punishment on illegal aliens.

text.p: Malaysia has imposed tougher penalties, including caning, on illegal immigrants and those responsible for bringing them into the country, local newspapers reported on Friday.

They quoted Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad as telling reporters on Thursday that the National Security Council has decided to take a tough stand to curb the influx of illegal immigrants. Mahathir is also the council's chairman.
"The existing laws are not enough. We want to be severe," he was quoted by the New Straits Times as saying.
"Illegal immigrants and whoever employ them will be severely dealt with, and the government had decided that they be caned," he said, adding that besides caning, they would also be deported.
Mahathir said surveillance along the coasts would be increased to prevent illegal immigrants from entering the country.
Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said last week that the government had stopped issuing permits allowing companies to import foreign labour.
He said there were 1.75 million foreign workers in Malaysia and one million of them were illegal immigrants.
Anwar said if companies needed foreign labour they could recruit illegal immigrants held temporarily at immigration depots before being deported.
